The refusal should read like `Ann Lee already has 2 bookings on 2026-03-02`.

Patients are upset at being charged the first time they miss an appointment. Add a `first_no_show_free` setting to the clinic file, default `true`: while it is on, each patient's first no-show (by phone number, earliest appointment first) carries no charge, and later no-shows are charged `no_show_fee` as before. With the setting `false`, every no-show is charged.

Our workshop adds a shop supplies charge to every job for rags, cleaners and small hardware, and fleetkeep has no way to record it. Each work order should carry a supplies charge of `shop_supplies_percent` percent of its labour, rounded to the cent and capped at `shop_supplies_cap` per work order. Make both fleet.ini settings, with defaults `5` and `40.00`. `fleetkeep wo show` should list the charge as `supplies` and include it in the work order's `total`.

The shop bills labour on our big trucks at a higher rate. Add a fleet.ini setting `heavy_labour_rate`, default `125.00`, and charge labour on `heavy` vehicles at that rate instead of `labour_rate`. A rate given with `--rate` on `fleetkeep wo labour` still takes precedence.

Drop-lowest drops the wrong score when a category's assignments are worth different amounts. A student with 4/5 on one quiz and 6/10 on another has the 4/5 dropped, because 4 points is fewer than 6, even though 60% is the worse result. Course grades should rank scores for drop-lowest by percent of possible points, not by points earned.

After a sensor is recalibrated we want to re-derive its old readings, but the readings log only keeps the calibrated value. Add the uncalibrated value to every row of the readings log as a new column `raw`, placed right after `value`, in the same unit and with the same decimals as `value`. The log's columns become `timestamp,zone,sensor,kind,value,raw,unit`.

When a probe fails, the controller writes `ERR` in the value column. `greenhouse ingest` rejects those rows today, so probe outages leave no trace in the readings log. Keep them instead: log each ERR row with an empty `value` and `raw`, and count it as a gap, neither imported nor rejected. The line `ingest` prints becomes `imported {imported} rows, {gaps} gaps, rejected {rejected}`.

The valve timers only take whole multiples of five minutes, so a suggestion like `gh1: 12 min` can't be keyed in as it is. Add a `timer_step_minutes` setting to `settings.json`, default `5`, and round every irrigation suggestion up to a whole multiple of it: 12 minutes becomes 15, 10 stays 10, and a zone that needs no water still gets 0.

When an agent tries to check a guest into a room housekeeping hasn't finished, `check_in` refuses with `Room 102 is not available` and the command line prints the same, so the agent has to go and find out why. Make the message give the room's housekeeping status: `Room {room} is not ready: {status}`, for example `Room 102 is not ready: dirty`.

In the rules file, a rule with `"match": "contains"` matches its pattern anywhere inside the payee (`substring, any case`), so my `BP` rule for Fuel also files `EBPAY ONLINE` and `BPAY BILLER` as fuel. Change `contains` to match `whole words, any case`: the pattern has to start and end at word boundaries in the payee, so `BP` still matches `BP 1234 LONDON` and `CARD PAYMENT BP` but no longer `EBPAY ONLINE`. For rules that relied on the old behaviour, add a new match kind, `anywhere`, that works exactly the way `contains` works today: `substring, any case`.

The month-end report lists only the top 5 payees, which hides most of a busy month. List the top `10` by default, and add a `--top` option to `report month` to choose another number, e.g. `--top 3`.

Members keep bringing books back a day or two late and then arguing about the small fines. Please add a grace period: a copy returned no more than `fine_grace_days` days after its due date is not fined at all. Make it a `lending.ini` option named `fine_grace_days`, default `2`. Past the grace period the fine still counts from the due date, so a book returned 3 days late pays for 3 days, as it does now.

Finance reconciles fines against the loans ledger and wants every charge on a line of its own. When a late return is fined, the `return` line should have amount `0.00` and be followed by a `fine` line with the same date, barcode, card and due date, carrying the fine as its amount. Returns without a fine get no `fine` line. Because older copies of the program would misread these files, new loans ledger files should start with `#lending-ledger v2` instead of `#lending-ledger v1`. Ledgers that already exist keep their `#lending-ledger v1` first line and must still open.

Members phone in to cancel holds they no longer want. Add `lend cancel-hold CARD TITLE`, where TITLE is the title id as `lend hold` takes it, which removes that member's hold on the title and prints `hold on {title} for {card} cancelled`. If a copy had already been set aside for them, it goes to the next member waiting for the title, or back on the shelf if nobody is. If the member has no hold on that title, refuse with code `no_hold` and the message `{card} has no hold on {title}`.

The bookkeeping tool we load pay-run files into (`runs/{period}.json`) keeps tripping over money written as decimal strings like "1012.50". Please write money in pay-run files as `integer cents` instead, so 1,012.50 becomes `101250`. That covers every money field in the file: each payslip's totals, the run's `totals`, and each line's `amount` and `rate`. Line hours stay as they are. Since the layout changes, pay-run files written from now on should carry `"schema": 2`.

Thirds come out wrong. A recipe that calls for 1/3 cup of sugar shows `3/8 cup sugar` in `recipebox show`, and showing a 3-serving porridge made with 1 cup of oats at `--servings 1` gives `3/8 cup oats` as well. Amounts should be shown as halves, thirds, quarters or eighths, that is with the denominators `2, 3, 4, 8`, so both of those read `1/3 cup`.

Scripts that read our `library.json` have to parse ingredient amounts such as `"1 1/2"` themselves. Please save each ingredient's `amount` in `library.json` as a JSON `number` (`1.5`) instead of a `string`, keeping `null` for an ingredient without an amount. Libraries saved before this change still have to open. The file keeps `version` 1.

Make `rating` the question type name for scale questions: survey files that say `rating` should load as scale questions, and saving a survey should write `rating`. We have years of older survey files that say `scale`, and those must keep loading. The question types in a survey file are then `single, multi, rating, text`.
